nodes.name: Actor state, timers and ground controls
nodes.purpose: Per-actor update that owns the physics fields (positions, vertical and horizontal speed, gravity, lateral impulse), the shared effect-timer countdown, the ground-state restore, the scripted descent and the death dissolve

nodes.name: Surface height, containment and ground helpers
nodes.purpose: Helpers called from the actor update: vertical coupling to a moving surface height, spherical tether containment, gravity bands with vertical speed clamps, and the angle-between-actors test used by chase and hit logic

nodes.name: Vector and angle helpers
nodes.purpose: Flat-vector headings in degrees and in eight-bit angle units, plus the shortest signed turn used whenever two headings are compared

nodes.name: Chase camera aim and mode dispatch
nodes.purpose: Rebuilds yaw and pitch from the eye-to-actor offset, turns them into a forward basis, and picks the distance preset for the current view mode

nodes.name: Per-mode camera preset setters
nodes.purpose: Small setters that install a view mode distance pair, an outer distance and a tilt before the camera update reads them

nodes.name: Scripted actions and contact resolution
nodes.purpose: Action handlers driven by the script argument buffer that launch, bounce and stun other actors, and the single resolve step that turns a contact into a hit

nodes.name: Actor and camera data layout
nodes.purpose: The field layout the cards name: position, vertical and horizontal speed, gravity, lateral impulse, facing angles, health, immunity, run and jump locks, water flag and the per-actor camera pointer

cards.name: Ground state restore
cards.summary: One reset routine rewrites gravity, horizontal speed, the lateral impulse and the water flag, and sets a short run lock while the actor still has health.
cards.behavior: A small reset routine rewrites the values the movement code reads instead of trusting what the previous state left behind. It clears the water flag, a lateral impulse field and two other fields. When the actor still has health, it also zeroes two state bytes and sets the run lock to 6. A dead actor gets no run lock. It then sets gravity to 4.0 and horizontal speed to 15.0. The run lock is a short countdown, so the actor cannot sprint for a few updates after the reset. The caller context is not shown in this tree, so which transitions use it is unverified. Field names are unknown in this decompiled source, so the roles below come from how the code uses them.

constants.name: restoredGravity
constants.unit: world units of downward acceleration per update; update rate unverified

constants.name: restoredSpeed
constants.unit: world units of horizontal travel per update; update rate unverified

constants.name: restoredRunLock
constants.unit: updates of the run lock; one unit consumed per update

cards.name: Steer by the side of the target angle
cards.summary: A steering call adds or subtracts a lateral impulse depending on which side of the actor the target angle lies.
cards.behavior: Steering is a sideways impulse, not a direct heading write. The call takes a target angle, a magnitude and a gain, and the gain is first multiplied by a global scale value. It writes a second facing value in degrees, from the actor facing plus a quarter turn times 360 over 65536. It then tests the signed difference between the target and the current facing, shifted by the same quarter turn. If the half-turn bit of that difference is set, the lateral impulse falls by magnitude times gain. Otherwise it rises by that amount. The single mask test covers the whole circle with no wrap arithmetic. The impulse field is the same one that the ground reset clears and the stomp bounce sets. Field names are unknown in this decompiled source, so the roles below come from how the code uses them.

constants.name: quarterTurn
constants.unit: angle units of a 65536-step turn; applied per update

constants.name: degreesPerAngleUnit
constants.unit: degrees per angle unit (360 divided by 65536); applied per update

constants.name: halfTurnMask
constants.unit: 16-bit angle mask; tested once per steering update

cards.name: Facing chase with a one-unit floor
cards.summary: Each update one signed 16-bit field moves a twelfth of its gap toward another, plus one unit toward the target, clamped so it cannot overshoot.
cards.behavior: A proportional chase moves one signed 16-bit field toward a second one. Each update, the step is the gap divided by 12 with integer truncation, plus one extra unit in the direction of the target. The result is clamped so it cannot pass the target. The first update closes about eight percent of a large gap, and about two thirds of the gap is gone after twelve updates. The extra unit makes small gaps finish instead of stalling on truncation. The step does not use the update delta, so this is per-update smoothing and a slow frame makes the turn lag. The code does not wrap angles, so a gap that crosses the 16-bit seam is chased the long way. The fields are probably a current and a target facing, but the names are unknown in this tree.

constants.name: gapDivisor
constants.unit: angle units of the chase divisor, one step per update (12 decimal)

constants.name: minimumStep
constants.unit: angle units added per update so small gaps finish

cards.name: Effect timer convention
cards.summary: Run, jump and immunity locks share one countdown: zero means finished, 255 means held, every other value drops by the update delta, and the run lock treats 250 and above as held too.
cards.behavior: Timed effects on an actor share one convention. The run lock, the jump lock, the immunity counter and one more byte counter are decremented by a per-update step value that is read from a global byte, so a longer update consumes more units. Each of these clamps to zero instead of wrapping. Zero means the effect is over and the field is left alone. For the jump lock and immunity, 255 means held forever, because the countdown branch skips it. The run lock treats any value from 250 up as held. A few other counters, such as a chase timer and an interaction timer, subtract the same step only while positive and can end below zero. Two further byte counters decrement by exactly one. A caller only has to test for non-zero to know whether a clamped lock is live.

constants.name: heldValue
constants.unit: timer units; 255 is held and never decremented, read per update

constants.name: heldRunThreshold
constants.unit: timer units; 250 and above are held, tested per update

capabilities: one countdown helper for every effect

cards.name: Fall past the stored floor
cards.summary: A vertical state lowers the actor by a fixed global step each update and exits when it is more than 100 units below a stored floor height.
cards.behavior: One vertical state does not integrate velocity. Each update it subtracts a global per-update vertical step from the actor height. It also sets a flag bit on the actor. It compares the height with a stored floor height for that actor. When the actor is more than 100 world units below that value, the state calls the shared state-exit routine with a zero argument. The 100 units act as a pit margin: a stored floor that is slightly high does not end the state early. The meaning and units of the global step are not named in this tree. Field names are unknown in this decompiled source, so the roles below come from how the code uses them.

constants.name: pitMargin
constants.unit: world units below the stored floor height; checked per update

cards.name: Death dissolve countdown
cards.summary: A dying actor counts up by the update delta while its scales and horizontal speed decay by 0.95 each update, then locks into a dead state with zeroed motion at 141 units.
cards.behavior: Dying is a countdown, not a switch. Each update the counter gains the per-update step value, and while it is below 141 the horizontal scale, the vertical scale and the horizontal speed are all multiplied by 0.95. Health is also forced to zero on those updates. With a step of one, the character ends at about 0.07 percent of its starting size. When the counter reaches 141, the actor is locked out. The routine sets bits in a global per-actor mask, sets immunity, stun and run lock to 255, raises a state flag, zeroes velocity and gravity, and sets the interaction state to 5. The threshold test returns early, so the lockout runs once and the decay stops. This gives a fade instead of a pop, and the 0.95 factor sets how long it feels. Field names are unknown in this decompiled source, so the roles below come from how the code uses them.

constants.name: dissolveUnits
constants.unit: timer units added by the update delta (141 decimal), one count per update

constants.name: decayFactor
constants.unit: multiplier on both scales and on horizontal speed; applied per update

cards.name: Heading from a flat direction
cards.summary: Two helpers turn a flat direction vector into a bearing, one in degrees and one in 256-step byte units.
cards.behavior: The degree helper takes the horizontal pair of a vector, returns zero for zero length, and otherwise divides the negated x by the horizontal length. It passes the result to an approximate inverse cosine and scales the angle to degrees. It then uses 270 minus the angle when z is positive, and 90 plus the angle otherwise. It subtracts 90 and adds 360 to a negative result, giving a bearing in 0 to 360 degrees. The byte helper does the same flat projection with the unnegated x. It uses an approximate inverse cosine in 256-step units. When z is positive, it mirrors the result around 128 for values below 64, and around 384 otherwise. It also returns zero for zero length. Both ignore the vertical component, so jumping does not change the bearing. Field names are unknown in this decompiled source, so the roles below come from how the code uses them.

constants.name: positiveZOffset
constants.unit: degrees; evaluated per heading query, once per actor per update

constants.name: negativeZOffset
constants.unit: degrees; evaluated per heading query

constants.name: finalShift
constants.unit: degrees subtracted after the sign fold; evaluated per heading query

constants.name: fullTurn
constants.unit: degrees added to negative bearings; evaluated per heading query

constants.name: byteQuarter
constants.unit: eight-bit angle units, the mirror boundary; tested per heading query

constants.name: byteUpperMirror
constants.unit: eight-bit angle units used above a quarter turn; evaluated per heading query

cards.name: Shortest signed turn between angles
cards.summary: Two helpers return the signed shortest difference between two angles, one in floating degrees and one in integer degrees.
cards.behavior: Comparing headings needs the short way round the circle. The float helper subtracts the two angles. When the difference is above 180, it moves the first angle back by 360. When the difference is minus 180 or lower, it moves the second angle back by 360 instead. It returns second minus first, which lies inside a half turn and carries the sign of the turn. The integer helper uses the same rule in whole degrees. Its thresholds of 181 and minus 179 match the float boundaries at integer steps. Without the helper, a one degree correction across the 0 and 360 seam would read as a 359 degree swing.

constants.name: halfTurn
constants.unit: degrees, the upper wrap threshold; evaluated per angle comparison

constants.name: fullTurn
constants.unit: degrees removed from the wrapped angle; evaluated per angle comparison

constants.name: negativeHalfTurn
constants.unit: degrees, the lower wrap threshold; evaluated per angle comparison

constants.name: integerUpperBound
constants.unit: whole degrees, difference at or above this wraps the first angle; evaluated per angle comparison

constants.name: integerLowerBound
constants.unit: whole degrees, difference below this wraps the second angle; evaluated per angle comparison

cards.name: Camera aim from the eye-to-actor offset
cards.summary: Yaw is the bearing of the flattened eye-to-actor offset, pitch is the height difference over the horizontal distance wrapped into half a turn, and the look direction is rebuilt from both with sine and cosine.
cards.behavior: The camera aim is rebuilt every update from stored positions. Yaw is the bearing of the horizontal offset between two stored points, computed with the same flat-vector bearing helper as the actors, and scaled to radians. Pitch is the angle of the height difference over the horizontal distance, scaled to degrees. A value above 180 loses 360. It is then negated, reduced by one stored bias, increased by another, and scaled to radians. The forward direction is sine yaw times cosine pitch on one horizontal axis, minus sine pitch on the vertical axis, and cosine yaw times cosine pitch on the other horizontal axis. This is the standard yaw-then-pitch basis. Which stored point is the eye and which is the target is not named in this tree. Field names are unknown in this decompiled source, so the roles below come from how the code uses them.

constants.name: pitchWrap
constants.unit: degrees, the point past which a full turn is removed; applied per camera update

constants.name: fullTurn
constants.unit: degrees removed from an over-wrapped pitch; applied per camera update

cards.name: Camera mode presets
cards.summary: Each view mode installs a near distance pair and a larger outer distance; the tightest special case is 40 and 40 with an outer 150, the widest 500 and 500 with an outer 800.
cards.behavior: Camera views are chosen as presets, not solved from scratch. A dispatcher reads a view-mode index into a preset table. It copies one table entry into an outer value, and the other into both members of a pair, which the code uses like a near value. Special states override this. A mode bit with a held button gives 40 and 40 with an outer value of 150. A mode bit without the button rebuilds the near value from a stored height difference. A flag on the tracked actor gives 40 and 40 with an outer value of 194. A third branch that also tests the mode bit can never run, because the branch before it already takes every case with that bit set. Scene setup calls dedicated setters. They write 500 and 500 with 800 for a wide view, 117 and 117 with 370 for a close view, and 230 and 230 with 290 for a mid view. Two more setters also write a tilt field. One writes minus 38 degrees with 143, 143 and 150. The other writes 30 degrees into two fields with 155, 155 and 178. The table values themselves are not in this source. Field names are unknown in this decompiled source, so the roles below come from how the code uses them. The values act like camera distances, but the unit is not stated.

constants.unit: world units of view distance; written once per mode change

constants.name: tightOuter
constants.unit: world units of outer view distance; written once per mode change

constants.name: actorFlagOuter
constants.unit: world units of outer view distance; written once per mode change

constants.name: wideNear
constants.unit: world units of view distance; written once per mode change

constants.name: wideOuter
constants.unit: world units of outer view distance; written once per mode change

constants.name: closeNear
constants.unit: world units of view distance; written once per mode change

constants.name: closeOuter
constants.unit: world units of outer view distance; written once per mode change

constants.name: chaseTilt

cards.name: Bounce off a stomped target
cards.summary: A bounce sets vertical speed to 12 and gravity to 5, and adds a lateral push of 5 mirrored against the current horizontal speed direction.
cards.behavior: A small callback sets the bounce after a hit on a target. Vertical speed becomes 12 and gravity becomes 5. The lateral impulse field is set to 5, or to minus 5 when the current horizontal speed is above zero. A moving actor is therefore pushed backward. A single function owns all of these writes, so every caller produces the same hop. This tree does not show which contact calls it, and the update rate for the speeds is unverified. Field names are unknown in this decompiled source, so the roles below come from how the code uses them.

constants.name: bounceSpeed
constants.unit: world units of upward travel per update; update rate unverified

constants.name: bounceGravity
constants.unit: world units of downward acceleration per update

constants.name: recoilPush
constants.unit: world units per update of lateral push; sign chosen once per bounce

cards.name: Scripted launch and stun
cards.summary: A launch action stamps horizontal 18, vertical 40 and gravity 6 on its target, copies the attacker facing and stuns it at 254; one target id gets its motion zeroed instead.
cards.behavior: One action in a scripted set launches a target. It resolves the target from the actor target index, minus 100, and acts only when a state byte on the target is at least 100. It then clears that byte and writes a velocity triple: horizontal speed 18, vertical speed 40, and gravity 6. It copies the attacker facing onto the target and clears one counter. It sets the stun byte to 254, clears another counter and sets a third from a helper call. It sets a field to 0xFFFF and raises a flag bit. When the target id equals 0x20, all three velocity values are zeroed and a different flag is raised, so that target stays in place. The target index is cleared on every call. The gravity is part of the action, not of the target. The speed unit and update rate are unverified. Field names are unknown in this decompiled source, so the roles below come from how the code uses them.

constants.name: launchSpeed
constants.unit: world units of horizontal travel per update; update rate unverified

constants.name: launchUp
constants.unit: world units of upward travel per update

constants.name: launchGravity
constants.unit: world units of downward acceleration per update

constants.name: stunValue
constants.unit: stun units; 254 is written once per launch and held per update

cards.name: Immunity split on contact
cards.summary: Contact gives the attacker 255 immunity, a held value that never ticks, and the victim 200 units that count down by the update delta.
cards.behavior: Three contact handlers use the same immunity write. When the second actor argument is in interaction state 1, the first actor gets an immunity of 255 and the second gets 200. They also set a shared global value and call one common routine. 255 is the held value in the timer convention, so the first actor stays immune until something clears the field. The second actor count falls by the per-update step, so it returns to vulnerable after roughly 200 steps. At one step per update and 60 updates per second, that is about three seconds. One handler sets a different global value for one particular actor id. The roles of the two actors are not named in this tree. Field names are unknown in this decompiled source, so the roles below come from how the code uses them.

constants.name: attackerHeldImmunity
constants.unit: immunity units; 255 is held and never decremented per update

constants.name: victimWindow
constants.unit: immunity units (200 decimal); one consumed per update

cards.name: Kill-hit resolution
cards.summary: A hit handler zeroes the target health, switches it to state 8 and writes result code 39, except for one exempt target id.
cards.behavior: One hit handler resolves a hit from one actor on another. When the target id is 0x88 and a field on the attacker is below 55, another field on the attacker gains 3. The shared hit routine then runs. Unless the target id is 0x53, the handler calls a helper, sets the target health to zero, switches the target to state 8, and writes 39 into the caller result byte. Only one handler of this shape is shown, so the full set of attack results is unverified. Field names are unknown in this decompiled source, so the roles below come from how the code uses them.

constants.name: comboCap
constants.unit: counter units (55 decimal); compared once per hit

constants.name: comboStep
constants.unit: counter units added per qualifying hit

constants.name: stateIndex
constants.unit: state index handed to the state changer; written once per killing hit

constants.name: resultCode
constants.unit: code written to the caller result byte; written once per hit

cards.name: Follow a changing surface height
cards.summary: An actor springs vertically with a surface height that moves at most 30 world units per update, moving by twice the gap to a point 230 units below it, capped at 300.
cards.behavior: An actor follows a changing surface height through a spring-like rule. The helper keeps the surface height of the previous update and subtracts it from the current one to get this update movement. It computes a gap equal to twice the distance between the actor and a point 230 units below the surface. A negative gap, an actor further below that point, does nothing. A surface movement larger than 30 units in one update is ignored, so a jump in the surface cannot fling the actor. Otherwise the gap is capped at 300, and the actor moves vertically by gap times surface movement times a gain taken from a global value that is not defined in this tree. The 230 is written as 60 plus 170. A rising surface lifts the actor and a falling surface lowers it. Field names are unknown in this decompiled source, so the roles below come from how the code uses them.

constants.name: surfaceGate
constants.unit: world units of surface travel per update; larger moves are ignored

constants.name: offsetLow
constants.unit: world units, first part of the 230-unit gap; applied per update

constants.name: offsetHigh
constants.unit: world units, second part of the 230-unit gap; applied per update

constants.name: gapCap
constants.unit: world units, the largest gap used; applied per update

constants.name: gapResponse
constants.unit: multiplier on the gap before the gain; applied per update

cards.name: Tether radius clamp
cards.summary: With a tether index set, an actor is held inside a sphere of eight world units per index around a table point, and rewritten onto that radius when it strays outside.
cards.behavior: One containment state ties an actor to a point stored in a scene table. When the actor tether index is not zero, each update it measures the 3D distance to that point and adds a small global constant inside the square root, so a coincident actor does not divide by zero. The radius is the tether index times 8 world units. If the actor is outside the radius, its position is rewritten to the point plus the unit direction times the radius. The actor therefore stays on the sphere and keeps its direction from the anchor, and an index of zero turns the constraint off. The distance is 3D, so the limit is a sphere, not a cylinder. Field names are unknown in this decompiled source, so the roles below come from how the code uses them.

constants.name: radiusStep
constants.unit: world units of radius per tether index; clamp checked per update
